tasks.short: Patrol refinery units and assess conditions

steps.what: Patrol units, monitor storage tank amounts and assess actual activities against applicable operating requirements

tasks.design: Retain the physical patrol and contextual verification of activities. Native indications in {OPS_SYSTEM} support observation, while controlled requirements in {DOCS} support interpretation; record automation does not establish a compliant or safe unit.
tasks.previous_blocker: A patrol observes actual conditions and activity beyond individual numerical values.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital rounds can record findings, but the task establishes no separate record-preparation share to remove.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected activity and inconsistent indications require operator judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize a mismatch between displayed state and what is happening in the unit.
tasks.altitude: Protect direct patrol and operational assessment time.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of production and operating workers
reach.learn: Which contextual observations require responsible operational review

evidence.claim: AVEVA Mobile Operator supports digital rounds feeding a historian; this does not establish replacement of physical patrol or conformity judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is patrol and verification, excluding independent compliance audit, corrective control actions and separate report preparation. Shared gauge observation with the gauge task is assigned once.

Responsible plant personnel supply current requirements before patrol; instruments and actual activities produce observations during s1. The operator inspects and clarifies within retained time. No free safe-unit, efficient-operation or regulation-compliant flag is assumed.
Use existing rounds and native indications first. No new sensing, delegated capture or added maintenance is proposed.
unknowns: Actual patrol obligations and instrument coverage
research_questions: Which patrol findings require observation beyond available numerical indications?

steps.what: Plan product movement through interconnected processing, storage and shipping units using verified operating context

tasks.design: Keep movement planning with the operator using current {OPS_SYSTEM} indications and controlled information in {DOCS}. This design does not infer route availability or issue plant control commands from a schedule.
tasks.previous_blocker: Interconnections, capacity and product constraints must be reconciled with actual operating context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing information supports planning but supplies no validated automatic replacement in the digest.
tasks.still_hard: A nominally connected route may be unsuitable or unavailable in the actual situation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize unresolved constraints and seek the responsible operational clarification.
tasks.altitude: Movement planning retains its full human time.

reach.learn: How receiving-unit context affects a proposed movement

evidence.claim: Product movement planning requires contextual operational judgement; no local automatic planning saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is planning, excluding plant switching, permits, actual pumping and separate engineering capacity studies.

Production planning supplies movement requirements and responsible operators supply current unit constraints before the plan closes in s1. The focal operator checks source versions, units, current relevance and uncertainty within retained time. No free route-open, capacity-available or product-compatible flag is assumed; unresolved conditions remain questions.
Use native plant information and existing communication first. No new topology model, extra source-owner reporting or upkeep is proposed.
unknowns: Actual planning authority and current operating information
research_questions: Which movement constraints cannot be settled from nominal system diagrams alone?

tasks.short: Read automatic tank gauges at required intervals

steps.what: Verify tank gauge identities, required intervals and the applicability of available readings
Present supported automatic gauge readings by tank and required observation interval
outputs: time-linked flow and tank-amount reading view

steps.what: Read the combined gauge view, determine flow and tank amount and investigate uncertain indications
inputs: time-linked flow and tank-amount reading view
outputs: operator understanding of current indicated flow and tank amount

tasks.design: For existing supported gauges, configure a read-only interval view in {OPS_SYSTEM} from the native historian in {DATA_PLATFORM}. Reduce repeated separate retrieval while retaining source applicability checks and operator interpretation; this view provides no plant control or automatic safety conclusion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reading multiple existing automatic displays can require repeated retrieval of the same interval's values.
tasks.enabler_now: Native historian integration can present time-linked instrument readings without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Stale data, mismatched tags and uncertain instruments can make a combined view misleading.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize that a displayed number may not represent a reliable current tank condition.
tasks.altitude: Use a combined read-only view while retaining periodic attention and interpretation.

reach.role: inspector, tester, sorter, sampler or weigher
reach.learn: How source identity and observation time limit a measurement conclusion

evidence.claim: AVEVA Mobile Operator and PI support operational readings and historian use, but the digest does not establish compatibility with this plant's specific tank gauges.
The proposed read-only gauge view and local retrieval savings are unmeasured E1, conditional on an existing usable instrument stream.

assumptions: Boundary is scheduled reading and determining indicated flow/amount, excluding patrol, instrument calibration, safety functions and control actions. No physical round is removed when still required. Shared observations with patrol are assigned once.

Producer contract: existing automatic instruments and their controller/historian produce tag ID, measured value, unit, source timestamp and native quality status before s2 for each required interval. Controls personnel verify tag-to-tank mapping, units and freshness behavior during commissioning, with their effort counted below; no new sensor or valid-reading flag is assumed. In s1 the operator captures required tank/tag set, interval, source version and known exceptions within its 20 hours. S3 retains comparison against actual indications and manual clarification.

Native historian views precede custom code. Stale or absent data, unverified mappings or gauges without supported output use the existing manual display reading route; if most reading is already central, savings are zero. The support estimate includes initial mapping effort amortized over the evaluated workload.
unknowns: Existing gauge stream contract and repeated retrieval burden
Which interval checks require physical attendance
research_questions: Does a verified combined view reduce retrieval effort after mapping, stale-data handling and retained reading obligations?

steps.what: Synchronize activities with other pumphouses through direct operational communication and current-condition clarification

tasks.design: Retain reciprocal operator coordination using existing {OPS_SYSTEM} context. A shared status display supports the exchange but does not establish another pumphouse's readiness or authorize a coordinated operation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Continuous flow and product separation depend on synchronized actual conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: The supplied record tools establish no validated substitute for this operational exchange.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected timing and product conditions require clarification across operators.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize an unresolved dependency and ensure the other party understands the intended activity.
tasks.altitude: Cross-pumphouse coordination retains its full time.

reach.learn: How changing conditions affect reciprocal operating commitments

evidence.claim: Operational synchronization requires reciprocal context and judgement; a log or status display alone does not establish a local labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is communication and synchronization, excluding separate movement planning, permits and actual control actions. Overlapping planning conversations are assigned once.

Responsible planning supplies the applicable plan before s1; other pumphouse operators supply current conditions and responses during s1 before coordination closes. Clarification and existing capture remain retained. No free ready-pumphouse, contamination-cleared or agreed-start flag is assumed.
Existing communication and native state displays come first. No new reporting burden, automatic control system or upkeep is proposed.
unknowns: Actual coordination authority and cross-unit dependencies
research_questions: Which dependencies require direct clarification despite existing status visibility?
